{{Short description|Italian theoretical physicist}}
'''Erio Tosatti''' (born 9 November 1943 in [[Nonantola]]) is an Italian [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] active at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] (SISSA),  and at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)]], both in [[Trieste]], [[Italy]].  He is a broad-scope theorist who carried out research on a  wide range of [[condensed matter physics]] phenomena. His early work dealt with optical properties,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=GREENAWAY|first=D. L.|date=1969|title=Anisotropy of the Optical Constants and the Band Structure of Graphite|journal=Physical Review|volume=178|issue=3|pages=1340–1348|doi=10.1103/physrev.178.1340|bibcode=1969PhRv..178.1340G}}</ref> electron energy loss,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tosatti|first1=E.|last2=Bassani|first2=F.|date=1970-02-01|title=Optical constants of graphite|journal=Il Nuovo Cimento|volume=65|issue=2|pages=161–173|doi=10.1007/bf02711192|issn=0369-3554|bibcode=1970NCimB..65..161T|s2cid=118026306}}</ref> theory of [[exciton]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Harbeke|first=G.|date=1972|title=Band-Edge Excitons in Pb|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=28|issue=24|pages=1567–1570|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.28.1567|bibcode=1972PhRvL..28.1567H}}</ref> and nonlocal dielectric response <ref>{{Cite journal|last=Baldereschi|first=A.|date=1978|title=Mean-value point and dielectric properties of semiconductors and insulators|journal=Physical Review B|volume=17|issue=12|pages=4710–4717|doi=10.1103/physrevb.17.4710|bibcode=1978PhRvB..17.4710B}}</ref> in solids, including layer crystals such as [[graphite]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Harbeke|first=Gunther|date=1975|title=OPTICAL-PROPERTIES OF LAYER STRUCTURE COMPOUNDS|journal=RCA Review|volume=6| issue =  1|pages=40–69}}</ref> and [[semiconductor]]s; charge- and spin-density-waves;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tosatti|first1=E.|last2=Anderson|first2=P.W.|title=Two-dimensional excitonic insulators: Si and Ge (111) surfaces|journal=Solid State Communications|volume=14|issue=8|pages=773–777|doi=10.1016/0038-1098(74)90883-7|bibcode=1974SSCom..14..773T|year=1974}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/BFb0107376|chapter=Electronic superstructures of semiconductor surfaces and of layered transition-metal compounds|title=Festkörperprobleme|volume=15|pages=113–147|series=Advances in Solid State Physics|year=1975|last1=Tosatti|first1=Erio|isbn=978-3-528-08021-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tosatti |first1=E. |last2=Anderson |first2=P. More details of his current and past research activity can be found [https://sites.google.com/site/tosattierio/ here].

==Life==

Born of a peasant family,  he made it to the renowned [[:it:Istituto tecnico industriale Fermo Corni|Istituto tecnico industriale Fermo Corni]]  high school of [[Modena]], where his early subjects were  technical and practical—electronics, nuclear technology, etc. Skills that allowed him to earn a living as a [[technician]] in a [[Human Physiology|human physiology]] [[research laboratory]] while studying physics at the local [[:it:Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia|Universita' di Modena]].   Associated from boyhood to Modena's  renowned [[:it:Corale Gioachino Rossini|Societa' Corale Rossini]] directed by [http://www.coralerossini.it/storiacoralerossini.pdf Livio Borri] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331214418/http://www.coralerossini.it/storiacoralerossini.pdf |date=2016-03-31 }}, a great music teacher, he sang for some years [[opera]] and church music within the choir which included among others the young [[Luciano Pavarotti]].

His physics degree ([[:it:Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia|Universita' di Modena]] 1967) was on pion-nucleon [[phase shift]] dispersion relations, a subject suggested by [[:de:Daniele Amati|Daniele Amati]].  Admitted to doctoral studies in Pisa's famous [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]]  he switched to the burgeoning field of solid state physics in the freshly established research group of [[Franco Bassani|Franco G. Bassani]] working on the optical properties of semiconductors.  His  doctoral work (Scuola Normale Superiore, Pisa 1970) employed optical and electron energy loss data along with dispersion relations typical of [[Particle physics|high energy physics]]  to work out the  anisotropic dielectric tensor of graphite, later useful in the context of [[graphene]].

After serving as a weather forecast under-lieutenant  ([[Genio Aeronautico Ruolo Fisici|GARF]]) for his (then compulsory) military service in the [[Italian Air Force]],  he moved to [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]]—where he also collaborated with [[Ugo Fano]]—with a researcher position of Italy's [[National Research Council (Italy)|National Research Council (CNR)]] .  That position allowed him freedom to leave for a joint 18-month long  [[Royal Society]] -  [[NATO]] fellowship to the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], at the [[University of Cambridge]], UK, where in 1972-73 he collaborated with [[Philip Warren Anderson|Philip W. Anderson]]. He also spent most of 1974 with a [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] fellowship at the [[University of Stuttgart]] in the group of [[Hermann Haken]] and most of 1977 at [[Stanford University]], in the group of [[Sebastian Doniach]] .

From [[Rome]] he was called to Trieste in 1977 by [[Abdus Salam]] and [[Paolo Budinich]] to start within the  [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]]  the  ICTP Condensed Matter Theory Group, now flourishing. In 1980 he also became a professor at the newly established  [[International School for Advanced Studies]] [[Www.sissa.it|(SISSA)]], where he founded and directed for 27 years the Condensed Matter Theory group, and where he still works.  From 1977 onwards his double involvement with SISSA and ICTP kept him in Trieste, with the exception of a sabbatical year at the [[IBM Research – Zurich|IBM Zurich Research Laboratory]] where in 1984-85 he also collaborated with [[K. Alex Muller]], as well as with [[Heinrich Rohrer]] and [[Gerd Binnig]].  His strong connection to the  ICTP  also brought him to serve as  Director in 2002–2003.

==Honors==

Tosatti was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2001, a corresponding member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] in 2006,  a foreign member of the [[National Academy of Sciences|U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] in 2011, a member of the [http://www.istitutolombardo.it/ Accademia Istituto Lombardo] in 2012,  a winner of the 2018 Enrico Fermi Prize of the [[Italian Physical Society]], https://en.sif.it/activities/fermi_award and in 2019 a foreign member of the  [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], the only Italian to be so honored.

For his research he  had also been awarded the [https://www.lrsm.upenn.edu/events/past-series-lectures/ Burstein Lecture] of the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1994, the [http://www.visitcomo.eu/export/sites/default/it/scoprire/alessandro-volta/allegati/Premio-per-la-fisica-francesco-somaini-fondazione-somaini.pdf Francesco Somaini Prize] in 1997, and a vast number of invited colloquia and named lectures worldwide.

For  his long-lasting efforts in favor of scientists in less fortunate countries  he was awarded the 2005 [https://www.aip.org/aip/awards/tate-medal AIP Tate Medal] whose citation states that [Tosatti] "has probably left much deeper marks in many countries than most of the programs that make the headlines".  For these merits the [https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/spirit-of-abdus-salam-award.aspx Spirit of Abdus Salam award] was also bestowed upon him in August 2020.
